result.rationale: Server schema addGuests.schema.ts is only z.array(z.string().email()) with no uniqueness refine, while AddGuestsDialog.tsx defines a client-only refinement requiring unique emails. The handler's uniqueGuests filter checks only against existing booking.attendees and the blacklist, not against duplicates within the input guests array, so createMany would insert duplicate Attendee rows for repeated emails from any non-dialog caller. The mechanism is verifiable in the diff.

judged_text: The server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema omits the uniqueness refinement that the client-side copy in AddGuestsDialog.tsx (lines 26-29) enforces, so the two copies of the same validation already disagree in this diff. Any caller other than this dialog (direct tRPC mutation, API client, or a stale bundle) sending guests:["a@b.com","a@b.com"] passes server validation, and createMany inserts two identical Attendee rows for one person, who then receives duplicate emails and appears twice in the calendar event; the client-side guard was the only thing preventing it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two different validations for the same input: client-side `AddGuestsDialog` defines `ZAddGuestsInputSchema = z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)` enforcing uniqueness, but server-side `packages/trpc/.../addGuests.schema.ts` only uses `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out existing booking attendees and blacklisted emails, but does not dedupe duplicates within the `guests` input itself, so `guests:["a@b.com","a@b.com"]` can reach `createMany` and create duplicate attendee rows (and then `attendeesList`/calendar event can include duplicates). This is a correctness defect exposed by the diff because the server trusts potentially duplicated input.
